body:
## Problem / outcome
ProxyLens must provide authorized group/application usage views without becoming a second CLIProxyAPI queue consumer or authoritative usage ledger.

## Scope
Implement a worker that reads CPAMP durable history through the approved adapter and maintains a rebuildable PostgreSQL projection:

- incremental refresh and full rebuild;
- CPAMP/native ID lineage;
- raw-field preservation plus normalized exclusive token buckets;
- requested and resolved model identity;
- estimated/authoritative cost classification;
- group/application attribution from validated correlation;
- freshness and adapter health states;
- stale/degraded/unavailable behavior;
- orphaned-group handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The worker reads only through the CPAMP adapter and never consumes the CLIProxyAPI queue.
- [ ] Projection rows retain CPAMP record IDs and all available native request IDs.
- [ ] Raw token fields and normalized mutually exclusive buckets are stored separately.
- [ ] Requested alias and resolved provider/model are retained separately.
- [ ] Cost includes amount, currency, pricing version, and estimated/authoritative classification when available.
- [ ] Correlation statuses distinguish correlated, partial, missing, duplicate, and ambiguous records.
- [ ] Uncorrelated records are not assigned to a group by guesswork.
- [ ] Incremental refresh and full rebuild produce equivalent projection results.
- [ ] Normal operation targets freshness within 60 seconds and exposes last-successful-sync time.
- [ ] Failed refresh keeps the last valid projection but marks it stale.
- [ ] Missing data is never represented as zero usage.
- [ ] Group-scoped queries enforce Keycloak group authorization.
- [ ] Missing Keycloak groups produce orphaned resources/projection status without silent reassignment.

## Non-goals

- Queue consumption by ProxyLens.
- Replacing CPAMP analytics.
- Billing or authoritative provider-cost settlement.
- Hard usage budgets before freshness/correlation validation.
title: CPAMP projection worker: rebuildable group-scoped usage views

body:
## Problem / outcome
ProxyLens needs a small resource model for group-owned applications and machine credentials without duplicating Keycloak identity or membership management.

## Scope
Implement application, client-key, and policy management:

- applications owned by exactly one Keycloak group;
- client keys owned by one application/group;
- one-time key reveal, prefix, hash, expiry, rotation, and revocation;
- group-admin/platform-admin authorization;
- group/application policies with narrowing-only inheritance;
- audit events for lifecycle changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An application cannot be created for a missing or orphaned group.
- [ ] An application and every client key have exactly one group owner.
- [ ] Group administrators can manage only resources in their validated groups.
- [ ] Platform administrators can manage resources across groups.
- [ ] Client-key plaintext is shown only once and is never recoverable.
- [ ] Only a secure hash and non-secret prefix are persisted.
- [ ] Active, revoked, and expired states are enforced immediately.
- [ ] Rotation creates a replacement key without exposing the old plaintext.
- [ ] Revocation is auditable and rejects new traffic immediately.
- [ ] Application policy can narrow group policy but cannot broaden it.
- [ ] No applicable allowlist defaults to deny.
- [ ] Lifecycle and authorization-denial audit events include actor, group, resource, timestamp, and outcome.

## Non-goals

- User or group CRUD outside Keycloak.
- Arbitrary custom permission language.
- Token/cost budget enforcement.
title: Resource and policy management: applications, client keys, and group ownership

body:
## Problem / outcome
Operators need request observability with stable group/session attribution without placing authorization, billing, or sensitive model content in Langfuse.

## Scope
Implement asynchronous Langfuse export from ProxyLens request lineage and CPAMP-derived usage:

- one generation observation per model request;
- Keycloak subject/group, application, ProxyLens/CPA/CPAMP IDs;
- requested/resolved model, provider, endpoint, status, latency;
- normalized usage and cost classification;
- retry/backoff and local spool/dead-letter behavior;
- default redaction and non-blocking delivery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provider responses do not wait for Langfuse ingestion.
- [ ] Temporary Langfuse failures are retried with bounded backoff and durable local retry state.
- [ ] Permanent failures are observable and do not cause request replay.
- [ ] Default observations exclude prompts, outputs, OAuth tokens, management keys, client-key plaintext, authorization headers, and raw failure bodies.
- [ ] `userId` uses the validated Keycloak subject when available.
- [ ] `sessionId` uses an allowed client session ID or generated request/session correlation.
- [ ] Metadata includes group ID, application ID, ProxyLens request ID, CPA/CPAMP IDs, model/provider, status, latency, and correlation state.
- [ ] Usage buckets are mutually exclusive and cost is marked estimated unless authoritative.
- [ ] Export behavior is tested during Langfuse outage and worker restart.
- [ ] Content capture remains disabled unless a separate approved specification enables it.

## Non-goals

- Langfuse as authorization or billing source of truth.
- Raw prompt/output retention.
- Synchronous telemetry in the provider response path.
title: Langfuse exporter: redacted asynchronous request observations

body:
## Problem / outcome
Clients need an authorized API entry point that preserves the Codex-compatible request contract while keeping CLIProxyAPI and management credentials private.

## Scope
Implement the public ProxyLens gateway for the Phase 1 Codex path:

- client-key authentication using hashed keys;
- application/group/policy resolution;
- model/provider allowlists;
- request-size and timeout limits;
- per-key/application request-rate limits;
- service-managed CLIProxyAPI credential forwarding;
- request ID generation and propagation;
- streaming, tools, multimodal inputs, errors, disconnects, and retry rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Plaintext client keys are never stored or logged.
- [ ] A revoked, expired, unknown, or malformed key is rejected before upstream forwarding.
- [ ] Application ownership and Keycloak group scope are checked before forwarding.
- [ ] Policy denial produces a stable client error and no upstream request.
- [ ] Authorized Codex Responses-compatible requests reach CLIProxyAPI.
- [ ] Streaming begins without buffering the full response.
- [ ] Tools and multimodal payloads are preserved.
- [ ] Retries occur only before response bytes are sent; partial streams are not automatically retried.
- [ ] Client disconnect handling is implemented where upstream cancellation is supported.
- [ ] ProxyLens and CLIProxyAPI request IDs are emitted in safe response/log correlation fields.
- [ ] CLIProxyAPI Management API credentials are never exposed on the public path.

## Non-goals

- Provider OAuth implementation.
- Chat Completions or non-Codex protocols unless required by the validated adapter contract.
- Hard token/cost budgets.
- Direct end-user access to CLIProxyAPI or CPAMP.
title: ProxyLens gateway: client-key auth and Codex request forwarding

body:
## Problem / outcome
The single-host reference deployment needs explicit operational behavior before it can be used as a reliable POC or implementation baseline.

## Scope
Define and implement:

- separate audit/security events and usage projection data;
- default retention: 90 days for ProxyLens request/usage projections, 365 days for audit/security events, 90 days for Langfuse metadata observations;
- raw prompt/output disabled;
- backup and restore procedures;
- health and freshness metrics;
- restart, outage, stale-data, and orphaned-resource behavior;
- upgrade and rollback order;
- queue-loss monitoring through CPAMP rather than direct ProxyLens queue access.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retention defaults are configurable and documented.
- [ ] Usage, audit/security, and provider credential data have distinct retention treatment.
- [ ] Raw prompts and outputs are not persisted or exported in the default deployment.
- [ ] ProxyLens PostgreSQL, Keycloak, CLIProxyAPI credential/config, CPAMP history, and enabled Langfuse dependencies have documented backup/restore procedures.
- [ ] Restore order and post-restore validation are documented.
- [ ] Upgrade and rollback order is documented with version compatibility checks.
- [ ] Health checks expose Keycloak, CLIProxyAPI, CPAMP adapter, PostgreSQL, projection freshness, and Langfuse exporter state.
- [ ] CPAMP outage makes usage views stale/degraded without fabricating zeroes.
- [ ] Keycloak outage follows the approved active-token behavior and blocks new authentication/management operations.
- [ ] ProxyLens database failure prevents forwarding requests whose identity/authorization cannot be recorded.
- [ ] Orphaned resources are visible and unusable until explicitly reassigned or revoked.
- [ ] Audit events cover key lifecycle, policy changes, authorization denials, integration actions, reconciliation, exports, and deletion.

## Non-goals

- High availability.
- Multi-host orchestration.
- Cross-instance failover.
- Automated deletion from Keycloak or CPAMP-owned history.
title: Operational hardening: audit, retention, backup, outage, and recovery behavior

body:
## Problem / outcome
ProxyLens needs one authoritative identity and group-management system without duplicating users, memberships, or group administration locally.

## Scope
Integrate a self-hosted Keycloak deployment using one dedicated `proxylens` realm:

- browser/operator OIDC login;
- local JWT validation using Keycloak published keys;
- separate browser, API-audience, and confidential Admin API clients;
- ProxyLens client roles: `platform-admin`, `group-admin`, `group-member`, `auditor`;
- flat groups with stable group IDs;
- multi-group membership with union-of-scope authorization;
- reconciliation for missing/orphaned groups.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can authenticate through the configured OIDC flow.
- [ ] ProxyLens validates issuer, audience, signature, expiry, roles, and group claims locally.
- [ ] Keycloak Admin API credentials are server-side only.
- [ ] Role capability and group scope are enforced independently.
- [ ] Platform administrators can operate across groups.
- [ ] Group administrators can operate only within groups in their validated claims.
- [ ] Members can use permitted applications and view permitted usage but cannot manage keys.
- [ ] Auditors have read-only access.
- [ ] Nested groups are rejected or explicitly unsupported.
- [ ] Missing referenced groups are detected and resources become orphaned and unusable until reassigned or revoked.
- [ ] Keycloak outage behavior follows the documented token-validation policy.

## Non-goals

- External Keycloak integration.
- Local password storage or local membership tables.
- Nested-group inheritance.
- Automatic reassignment after group deletion.
title: Keycloak integration: realm, OIDC validation, roles, and group scope

body:
## Problem / outcome
ProxyLens must read authoritative CPAMP request history without consuming the CLIProxyAPI usage queue or creating a competing ledger. The supported CPAMP read/export surface is currently an open integration assumption.

## Scope
Investigate the deployed CPAMP Full Mode version and implement a small adapter proof of concept using this order:

1. supported CPAMP API/export/read interface;
2. explicitly enabled, version-pinned, read-only SQLite fallback only if no supported interface exists.

Document authentication, filtering, pagination/cursors, record IDs, timestamps, freshness, retention, error behavior, and version compatibility.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CPAMP Full Mode version and persistence contract are recorded.
- [ ] The adapter reads durable request history without calling or popping CLIProxyAPI's usage queue.
- [ ] The preferred supported interface is identified and exercised, or the fallback is explicitly documented as version-pinned/read-only.
- [ ] Returned records preserve CPAMP record ID, native CLIProxyAPI request ID when available, timestamps, provider, requested/resolved model, status, latency, raw token fields, normalized token fields, cost classification, and correlation metadata.
- [ ] Filtering/pagination behavior is tested.
- [ ] Adapter states expose available, stale, degraded, and unavailable conditions.
- [ ] CPAMP outage, malformed records, retention gaps, and duplicate reads are handled without fabricated usage.
- [ ] A short compatibility note is added to `DEVELOPMENT.md` or the relevant integration documentation.

## Non-goals

- Building tenant authorization or UI.
- Consuming the CLIProxyAPI queue from ProxyLens.
- Replacing CPAMP's analytics or durable history.
title: POC: verify CPAMP durable-history read/export contract

body:
## Problem / outcome
Tenant-scoped usage is only valid when a ProxyLens request can be joined reliably to its CLIProxyAPI request and CPAMP durable record. A shared upstream credential alone is not a tenant identity contract.

## Scope
Generate a ProxyLens request ID at ingress, propagate it through the supported request/header/metadata path, and test the resulting lineage across:

- ProxyLens request ID;
- CLIProxyAPI native request ID;
- CPAMP record ID;
- application and Keycloak group;
- Langfuse trace/session identifiers.

If the shared service-managed CPA credential cannot preserve reliable attribution, evaluate distinct application/group credentials as the fallback and record the resulting architecture decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The request lineage schema and lifecycle are documented.
- [ ] ProxyLens request ID propagation is implemented for the Codex Responses-compatible path.
- [ ] The POC demonstrates a deterministic join to CLIProxyAPI and CPAMP IDs, or records the exact unsupported hop.
- [ ] Correlation status is explicit: correlated, partial, missing, duplicate, or ambiguous.
- [ ] Duplicate and missing native IDs do not silently merge unrelated requests.
- [ ] The join preserves application and Keycloak group ownership.
- [ ] Langfuse receives the available native IDs and correlation status without secrets or raw content.
- [ ] Tenant-scoped usage is disabled when correlation is not proven.
- [ ] The result is recorded in `DEVELOPMENT.md` and, if the chosen mechanism is hard to reverse, an ADR is added.

## Non-goals

- General multi-provider correlation.
- Hard token/cost budget enforcement.
- Direct CLIProxyAPI queue consumption by ProxyLens.
title: POC: prove ProxyLens request correlation through CLIProxyAPI and CPAMP

body:
## Problem / outcome
The approved architecture requires a reproducible single-host deployment with explicit service boundaries, persistent state, private networking, and server-side credentials.

## Scope
Create the initial Docker Compose foundation for:

- Keycloak with one `proxylens` realm;
- ProxyLens API/gateway/worker placeholders or service entrypoints;
- CLIProxyAPI;
- CPAMP Full Mode;
- PostgreSQL for ProxyLens;
- optional Langfuse dependencies as enabled by the POC;
- private internal networks and only required published ports.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Images/builds are pinned to documented versions.
- [ ] Persistent volumes exist for Keycloak, CLIProxyAPI credentials/config, CPAMP history, ProxyLens PostgreSQL, and enabled Langfuse dependencies.
- [ ] Healthchecks and long-form dependency conditions are defined.
- [ ] Management keys, database passwords, Keycloak client secrets, and Langfuse credentials use Compose secrets or equivalent mounted secret files.
- [ ] CLIProxyAPI Management API and CPAMP manager/API ports are private.
- [ ] Only the approved gateway and operator/admin ports are published.
- [ ] A fresh host can start the stack from documented setup steps.
- [ ] Backup, restore, upgrade, and rollback order is documented.
- [ ] Failure behavior for dependency outage is documented.

## Non-goals

- High availability or multi-host scaling.
- Externally managed Keycloak.
- Production sizing claims.
- Provider OAuth flow implementation.
title: Compose foundation: Keycloak, CLIProxyAPI, CPAMP, PostgreSQL, and ProxyLens secrets

body:
## Problem / outcome
ProxyLens needs a validated single-host proof of concept before detailed product implementation. The POC must prove the approved ownership boundaries and the integration assumptions that cannot be inferred from architecture documents: Keycloak identity/group claims, Codex request forwarding, CPAMP durable-history reads, request correlation, derived usage projection, and redacted asynchronous Langfuse export.

## Scope
Build and validate one Docker Compose deployment containing:

- one self-hosted Keycloak `proxylens` realm;
- one CLIProxyAPI instance with one Codex OAuth provider account;
- one CPAMP Full Mode instance as the sole CLIProxyAPI usage-queue consumer;
- ProxyLens gateway/API/worker components;
- PostgreSQL for ProxyLens control-plane state and rebuildable projections;
- the selected Langfuse services or a compatible local Langfuse endpoint.

Use one flat Keycloak group, one application, and one ProxyLens client key.

## Required architecture constraints

- Keycloak is authoritative for users, authentication, groups, memberships, and group administration.
- CLIProxyAPI is authoritative for provider OAuth, credential runtime, model translation, routing, streaming, and tools.
- CPAMP Full Mode is the sole CLIProxyAPI usage-queue consumer and authoritative durable request-history/analytics service.
- ProxyLens must never independently pop the CLIProxyAPI usage queue.
- ProxyLens usage data is a rebuildable projection of CPAMP records.
- Raw prompts/responses are disabled; Langfuse export is redacted and non-blocking.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Compose stack starts with persistent volumes, private networks, healthchecks, pinned images, and Compose secrets.
- [ ] A Keycloak user can authenticate through OIDC; ProxyLens validates JWTs locally and resolves group/client-role claims.
- [ ] A ProxyLens client key authenticates one application owned by one Keycloak group.
- [ ] A Codex request passes through ProxyLens to CLIProxyAPI with Responses-compatible streaming, tools, and multimodal behavior preserved.
- [ ] CPAMP remains the only service consuming the CLIProxyAPI usage queue.
- [ ] The selected CPAMP read/export path returns durable request records without ProxyLens queue consumption; any SQLite fallback is explicitly version-pinned and read-only.
- [ ] A ProxyLens request ID is correlated to CLIProxyAPI and CPAMP native IDs, or the POC records the exact blocker and stops tenant-scoped usage claims.
- [ ] A group-scoped usage projection is shown only after correlation is proven and reports freshness within 60 seconds under normal operation.
- [ ] Projection states expose available, stale, degraded, and unavailable conditions; missing data is not shown as zero.
- [ ] Langfuse receives redacted metadata asynchronously and provider responses do not wait on Langfuse.
- [ ] Restart and outage scenarios are documented for Keycloak, CPAMP, ProxyLens PostgreSQL, and Langfuse.
- [ ] Backup, restore, upgrade, and rollback order is documented for the single-host deployment.

## Non-goals

- High availability or multi-host deployment.
- Multiple CLIProxyAPI/CPAMP connections or failover.
- Externally managed Keycloak integration.
- Nested Keycloak groups.
- Hard token/cost budgets before usage freshness and correlation are validated.
- Raw prompt/output retention.
- Provider support beyond the Codex POC path.

## Dependencies

This parent issue is decomposed into validation and implementation issues. CPAMP read/export and request-correlation validation are blocking gates for tenant-scoped usage.

## References

- `AGENTS.md`
- `GLOSSARY.md`
- `docs/adr/0001-architecture-boundaries.md`
- `docs/research/proxy-stack-research.md`
- `DEVELOPMENT.md`
title: Phase 1 POC: Keycloak, CLIProxyAPI, CPAMP, ProxyLens, and Langfuse
